newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon says anti-Israeli resistance to continue.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon says anti-Israeli resistance to continue.

text.p: Lebanon on Friday marked its 53rd independence day by saying a guerrilla war against Israeli forces in south Lebanon would not be stopped until the Jewish state's occupation of a border strip ended.

President Elias Hrawi, in a speech on Thursday night to mark the occasion, also said Lebanon was keen on Arab-Israeli peace and called for resumption of stalled peace talks on the basis of the land-for-peace formula of the 1991 Madrid peace conference.
"Liberating our occupied land in the south and the Western Bekaa is our sacred right," Hrawi said.
"It is our right to resist the occupation as we are a people that is keen on its dignity and sovereignty. The resistance will not stop except after the pullout of the occupation (forces)."

Guerrillas of the Hizbollah (Party of God) -- a Shi'ite Moslem faction funded and armed by Iran -- lead a guerrilla war against some 1,000 Israeli troops and 3,000 allied Lebanese militiamen occupying a south Lebanon border zone.

Israel waged a fierce 17-day blitz on Lebanon in April in a bid to crush Hizbollah, killing some 200 people, mostly civilians. A U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding that ended the blitz allows for guerrilla raids on Israeli forces in south Lebanon but bars both sides from targeting civilians.
Almost daily guerrilla attacks have killed 24 Israeli soldiers in south Lebanon this year.

Hrawi, other Lebanese leaders and foreign diplomats watched on Friday soldiers, tanks, armoured personnel carriers and heavy artillery roll along a former Beirut civil war frontline to mark the 53rd anniversary of independence from France.
Hrawi said Israel has no choice but to return to the negotiating table with the Lebanese and Syrians for some serious talking.

"We are keen on peace and we do not spare any effort to make it prevail over any other possibility...The freezing of the peace process is not in Lebanon's interest, nor in the interest of the region or even peace itself," Hrawi said.

"Israel has no choice but to stop its intransigence and return to serious negotiations leading to a peace based on the implementation of international resolutions, especially (Security Council) resolution 425 and the principle of land for peace," Hrawi said.

"It does not relate to peace when Israel impose on us to choose between a continuation of the occupation of our land or surrendering to its conditions. No to the continuation of occupation and no to surrender," he added.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejects resuming the talks on the basis of trading occupied Arab land for peace.
Resolution 425 calls for an unconditional Israeli pullout from the 15-km (nine-miles)-deep south Lebanon zone extending from Mount Hermon in the east to the Mediterranean westwards.

Hrawi reiterated that Beirut will continue close peace talks coordination with Damascus -- its main power broker with 35,000 troops stationed in Lebanon -- saying this formed "a guarantee to regain our land" in south Lebanon and the Golan Heights.
